subject: Priv infra: IaC stability & observability handback
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priv infra: IaC stability & observability handback

Hi team,

Quick context: Acme Ops asked for a short, prioritized list of IaC items we want them to validate before the next private deployment window. They also requested a minimal observability proposal so their SREs can reason about drift and failed runs in their on-prem VPC.

Can the infra leads review the attached draft checklist and the observability proposal and call out:
- blockers in our terraform state/config (remote backend, locking, partial states)
- helm/ansible divergence risks (secret templating, value pinning)
- CI gating gaps (what to gate at PR vs pipeline level)
- required runbook pages (what needs to exist on their Confluence before deploy)

I've attached: iac-drift-checklist.xlsx and privstack-observability-proposal.pdf as starting points. High level ask: produce a short annotated list (1 page) we can hand back to Acme by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Private Deployments (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: iac-drift-checklist.xlsx, privstack-observability-proposal.pdf

Subject: Re: Priv infra: IaC stability & observability handback

On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 09:12 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick context: Acme Ops asked for a short, prioritized list of IaC items we want them to validate before the next private deployment window.

Thanks Hannah — attaching the state access snippet and our backend details (see runbook_stub.txt). A few notes from our side after a quick pass:
- Terraform: we're using an S3-compatible backend with Dynamo-style locks. Please confirm the tfstate split strategy — currently single shared state for the whole privstack which makes partial apply harder.
- Helm: we keep two value sets (staging/prod) in the repo, but templated secrets are rendered at deploy time via our vault plugin. We can expose the vault paths but would prefer Redwood to avoid baking secret values into image artifacts.
- CI: we can enforce a pre-merge plan check step, but our runner quotas limit full plan runs on large modules. We propose a lightweight diffs-only check for PRs and a full plan in the gated pipeline.

We'll also add a small script to emit plan diffs as JSON so Redwood's automation can pick them up. Attaching runbook_stub.txt that lists who to call during an apply failure.

Files attached: runbook_stub.txt

— Alex (Acme Ops)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, ops@acme-corp.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-31T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra: IaC stability & observability handback

Thanks Alex / Hannah — quick technical responses and proposed edits to the checklist: 

1) Terraform state topology
- Recommendation: split state per environment + per-environment network/compute modules. Single global state is a risk for partial rollbacks and increases blast radius. If Acme wants to keep a single state we must add stricter locking and an automated state-backup step pre-apply (keep the last 5 versions).
- Add a validation step: terraform plan with -refresh -detailed-exitcode in the gated pipeline; bubble plan output to a signed artifact (we can use the plan-diff JSON Alex suggested).

2) Helm / Ansible divergence
- Concrete ask: add a 'values_hash' metadata file produced by CI for every helm release. This lets us detect divergent values between what was approved and what's actually deployed.
- For Ansible, avoid templating secrets inline. Use encrypted vault files referenced by variable names; CI should render and pass the secret via secure env, not commit secrets to repo.

3) Observability and drift detection
- Implement a periodic 'infra-convergence' check (cron job) that performs a plan-only run and emits a metric (drift_count) to Acme's Prometheus / push gateway. We should include a small exporter in the privstack observability proposal.
- Add alert thresholds and an incident runbook link (Confluence).

4) CI gating matrix (short table) — attached as comments in the spreadsheet.

I'll put these edits into the spreadsheet and the proposal. If Acme agrees to per-environment states, we'll update the runbook with the state restore procedure and test it in their staging cluster.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-31T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra: IaC stability & observability handback

All — thanks for the quick turn. Summary / decisions we will hand back to Acme tomorrow morning: 

- State topology: propose per-environment state (network, compute, infra) with automated pre-apply backup (5 snapshots). Owner: Marcus Lin.
- CI gating: implement PR-level lightweight diff + gated full plan in pipeline. Produce a plan-diff JSON artifact for audit. Owner: Aditya Rao.
- Helm/Ansible: add values_hash metadata for helm releases; require encrypted vault files for ansible variables, never commit decrypted secrets. Owner: Kimberly Park.
- Observability: add infra-convergence cron that runs plan-only and emits drift_count metric to Acme's Prometheus. We'll add alerts and link to Confluence runbook. Owner: Hannah (runbook coordination).

Action items before handback: Marcus to sketch state-split mapping and pre-apply backup steps (doc link: https://drive.google.com/privstack-observability-v1). Aditya to draft CI gating checklist and sample plan-diff output. Kim to update the spreadsheet with values_hash column and secret-handling guidance. I'll assemble and send the one-page handback and attach the runbook stub.

Acme Ops: if this plan is aligned we will schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the backup/restore test and the observability exporter. Proposed slot: Thu 10am PT. Can you confirm?

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Private Deployments (acting)
Redwood Inference
